text.en: Estu resizes a tiger picture. Images A, C and D look fine, but B looks stretched and E looks squashed. Why?

Pictures look similar when width and height change by the same factor, and distorted when they change by different factors.
A ratio compares two quantities; image A is 60 mm wide and 40 mm high, so its width-to-height ratio is 60 : 40.
The numbers in a ratio are its terms, and ratios whose terms change by the same factor are proportional.
To compare ratios, reduce each to its simplest form by dividing both terms by their common factor: 60 : 40 becomes 3 : 2.
Image D is 90 : 60, which also reduces to 3 : 2, so D is similar to A while a 60 : 30 image is 2 : 1 and looks stretched.
Proportional reasoning solves problems: if 3 notebooks cost 45 rupees, then 5 notebooks cost 45 ÷ 3 × 5 = 75 rupees.
To share an amount in a ratio, add the terms and divide: 100 rupees in the ratio 3 : 2 gives 60 and 40.
Unequal sharing needs parts: divide the whole by the total parts to get the value of one part.
Unit conversions use proportion too: 1 km = 1000 m, so 2.5 km = 2500 m.
Always check that both quantities in a ratio use the same unit before simplifying.

problem.en: Share 80 sweets between Asha and Ravi in the ratio 3 : 5.

why.en: Divide the whole by the parts.
Multiply each term by one part.

prompt.en: Why does image B look stretched when A, C, D do not?

requiredIdeas.en: Width and height must change by the same factor.
In B they change by different factors.

commonMisconceptions.en: A bigger picture is always similar.

points.en: A ratio compares two quantities; equal simplest ratios mean proportion.
Reduce a ratio by dividing both terms by a common factor.
Share a whole by adding the terms, finding one part and multiplying.
